headline: Tankers burn in Hormuz as Iran sets its terms for Washington
standfirst: Tehran reports five tankers hit by mines in the strait and sends, via Qatar, a nuclear proposal tied to seven demands. In Paraguay, President Santiago Peña resigns and is promptly impeached after a bank collapse, while in Somalia the Supreme Court rules the extension of the president's term unlawful.

essentials.title: Tankers hit by mines in Hormuz as Iran sets seven conditions for Washington
essentials.standfirst: Tehran says at least five tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, as the Pentagon stands ready for a resumption of fighting. Through Qatar, Iran has passed a proposal on its nuclear programme to the United States.
body: On Thursday 5 November Iranian forces reported at least five tankers and a tugboat ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz, most of them after striking mines on routes Tehran had not authorised; Britain's UKMTO agency also reported a vessel hit by two projectiles north of Qatar.

The same day, a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran had sent Washington, through Qatar, a proposal on its nuclear programme, to be discussed only once seven demands are met, among them the lifting of sanctions, the unfreezing of Iranian assets and war reparations.

The United States, which is studying the text, wants the nuclear issue on the table from the outset, and thousands of American troops stand ready to resume fighting, according to the New York Times, just as several of Donald Trump's allies distance themselves from the war after the defeat of 3 November.

impact.text: Oil prices feed through to the pump across Europe. In France, for example, diesel averaged €2.29 a litre in early November, according to AFP, despite the release of 10 million barrels from strategic stocks.

analysis.title: Seven conditions to reopen the strait
analysis.text: On a visit to Russia on Thursday, the senior Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei summed up Tehran's line: until its seven conditions are met, the Strait of Hormuz will stay shut and there will be no negotiation. Iran is betting on the weight of a passage through which about a fifth of the world's oil normally flows, and the Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, ruled out on Wednesday any "inclination to submit". In Washington the political mood has shifted: the vice-president, JD Vance, openly blames the electoral defeat on the war, the Republican senator Ted Cruz says it has gone on too long, and the Democrats, who will control Congress from January, want it ended.

keys.title: Qatar's role
keys.text: The emirate has carried messages between the two capitals since direct talks broke down. Its spokesman, Majed al-Ansari, says Washington and Tehran remain committed to the negotiating process and are studying the mediators' proposals.

keys.title: A mined strait
keys.text: Since late February Tehran has sharply restricted traffic through the strait, letting through only the ships it clears. UKMTO admits it is struggling to count the attacks, as most vessels no longer report them.

essentials.title: Paraguay's president, Santiago Peña, resigns and is impeached within minutes
essentials.standfirst: Brought down by the collapse of Ueno, a digital bank that claimed more than 60% of the country's adults as customers, the head of state announced his departure on Thursday. Deputies voted to impeach him straight afterwards.
body: On Thursday 5 November, in a video posted on X, Paraguay's president, Santiago Peña, announced his resignation in the name of "social peace" and institutional stability, minutes before the lower house voted by 78 to 0 to impeach him and send him for trial in the Senate.

His fall stems from the collapse of Ueno, a digital bank seized by the central bank on 3 November after poorly documented loans to firms linked to its owners came to light, and which held some $800m in public deposits; Horacio Cartes, leader of the Colorado Party, had already abandoned him.

Congress is due to rule on the resignation on Friday, which would allow the vice-president, Pedro Alliana, to be sworn in without awaiting a trial, while the opposition wants him removed from office, which would strip Mr Peña of the life seat in the Senate, with its legal immunity, reserved for former presidents.

analysis.title: A banking scandal at the top of the state
analysis.text: Born out of a former finance company, Ueno had become the country's digital bank of choice, with more than 70 branches. Its collapse cut off a large share of the population from their accounts, apps and cards overnight. The deposit-guarantee fund is due to repay up to about $36,000 per customer, which would cover 97% of depositors, according to the Associated Press. Eight executives have been detained, including the founder, Miguel Vázquez, and 27 people have been charged with breach of trust and attempted fraud. The attorney-general has opened three criminal investigations, which also target current and former officials, among them the president, who has apologised to Paraguayans and says he will co-operate.

keys.title: The succession
keys.text: The constitution hands the rest of the term, which runs until August 2028, to the vice-president, Pedro Alliana. A former speaker of the lower house and an ally of Horacio Cartes, he announced in April that he intended to run for president in 2028.

keys.title: A Trump ally
keys.text: Santiago Peña was one of the few foreign leaders to attend the American president's inauguration. The website Responsible Statecraft sees his fall as a setback for Washington's diplomatic push in Latin America.

essentials.title: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks, Russian and Ukrainian envoys meet at the White House
essentials.standfirst: Melania Trump brought together envoys from both countries in Washington on Thursday, with no progress announced. On the ground, Moscow is targeting Ukraine's energy and logistics networks while Kyiv steps up drone attacks on Russian refineries.
body: On Thursday 5 November the American first lady, Melania Trump, received Vladimir Putin's envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, and Russia's human-rights commissioner at the White House, along with two Ukrainian officials, including the head of the president's party, David Arakhamia, and urged them to look beyond a mere "temporary ceasefire".

The White House credits her with brokering a six-day truce in Oleshky, in the occupied Kherson region, which allowed nearly 800 civilians to be evacuated; the Russian strike of 2 November on an aid distribution in Komyshuvakha, which killed 43 people according to Kyiv, came the day after it expired.

The strikes go on: Moscow says it hit a depot of the Nova Poshta delivery company near Kharkiv and a cargo ship off Odesa, while more than 200 Ukrainian drones targeted the Ryazan region, ahead of three-way talks due in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.

analysis.title: An energy war
analysis.text: Each side is now going after the other's economy. According to Al Jazeera's Moscow correspondent, Ukraine has stepped up its strikes on Russian refineries, hitting Yaroslavl two days before Ryazan, where the governor, Pavel Malkov, counted more than 200 drones in a single night. Russia, for its part, is targeting electrical substations and logistics hubs, and Kyiv has endured rolling blackouts since mid-October as winter approaches. Melania Trump's humanitarian diplomacy runs alongside the main negotiating channel, that of the American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who spoke to Volodymyr Zelensky ahead of the Abu Dhabi meeting.

keys.title: The Abu Dhabi talks
keys.text: Ukrainian, Russian and American delegations are due to meet there on 10 and 11 November, at Washington's initiative. Three earlier rounds of talks, in Abu Dhabi and then Geneva, failed at the start of the year.

keys.title: Kyiv's position
keys.text: Volodymyr Zelensky insists that no deal can be struck without Ukraine and is demanding lasting security guarantees. Washington, which initiated this new round, is pressing both sides to conclude.

essentials.title: Herzog to name Israel's next prime minister on Sunday, with Gadi Eisenkot in pole position
essentials.standfirst: With 67 of the 120 members of the Knesset behind him, the former army chief awaits the mandate the president is due to hand out on 8 November. In Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, down to 46 backers, some cry "stolen" election.
body: After two days of consultations, Israel's president, Isaac Herzog, called the outcome "clear", with 67 of 120 members recommending Gadi Eisenkot against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu, but announced on Thursday 5 November that he would keep talking and would not award the mandate to form a government until Sunday.

That tally rests on an unprecedented alliance between the mainly Jewish opposition bloc and the two Arab parties: Ra'am, whose leader, Mansour Abbas, says he wants to enable an "emergency government", and the United List, which would back a minority government from outside.

In the outgoing camp positions are hardening: a minister from the far-right Otzma Yehudit party told the head of state that the election had been "stolen", although the electoral commission found no irregularities, and the new Knesset is due to be sworn in on 10 November.

analysis.title: Betting on a Jewish-Arab majority
analysis.text: Never before has a candidate for prime minister leaned so openly on the Arab parties, which together hold a record 19 seats. Without them, Gadi Eisenkot's bloc has only 48 members, well short of the 61 required. Likud has attacked the alliance, with its minister Yoav Kisch accusing the Arab parties of dedicating their victory to the people of Gaza, while Mansour Abbas wants an end to "loyalty tests" for his community. The outcome also hinges on the ultra-Orthodox: United Torah Judaism, which recommended no one, wants the exemption of yeshiva students from military service written into law, and Avigdor Lieberman, leader of Yisrael Beiteinu, says he is open to sitting with it, according to Channel 12.

keys.title: The timetable
keys.text: The president is due on Sunday to name the leader tasked with forming a government, who will have 28 days, extendable by 14. If no coalition emerges within the legal deadlines, voters would be sent back to the polls.

keys.title: Gaza, a truce that does not protect
keys.text: Despite the ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, nearly 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since, according to Gaza's health ministry. Donald Trump's peace plan remains largely stalled.

essentials.title: Somalia's Supreme Court rules the extension of the president's term unlawful
essentials.standfirst: The country's highest court on Thursday gave the parties thirty days to reach agreement and ninety days to hold elections. The day before, the head of state, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, had sacked the chief justice.
body: On Thursday 5 November the constitutional chamber of Somalia's Supreme Court ruled that the constitutional amendments adopted in March could extend neither the term of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, which expired on 15 May, nor that of parliament, and confined the federal government to a caretaker role.

The day before, the president had sacked the chief justice, Bashe Yusuf Ahmed, who was hearing an opposition challenge, and replaced him with a close ally, Ibrahim Idle Suleiman; the court declared the dismissal void, and the former prime minister Hassan Ali Khaire accuses the government of sending soldiers into the courthouse.

The judges demand an agreement between political parties within thirty days and elections within ninety, whereas the president meant to lead the country to its first direct elections, planned for April and May 2027, a reform whose terms the opposition and several regional parties dispute.

analysis.title: A political crisis amid an insurgency
analysis.text: The crisis could hardly come at a worse time for the country's security. Al-Shabaab, which is linked to al-Qaeda, controls large swathes of territory, and donors are cutting funding for the international military mission: Uganda, the biggest contributor to the African Union force, announced this week that it would withdraw all its troops by the end of 2027, and Washington has stopped funding a UN logistics mission, according to AFP. The UN's political mission in Somalia closed on 31 October. The dispute over the length of the president's term had already led to clashes between factions in Mogadishu in June. Hassan Sheikh Mohamud champions a reform meant to replace the clan-based electoral system with universal suffrage.

keys.title: The disputed reform
keys.text: Passed by parliament in March, the amendments lengthen terms of office and pave the way for universal suffrage. The opposition and regional parties boycotted the vote, some saying they had been prevented from taking part.

keys.title: The Galmudug precedent
keys.text: Under Bashe Yusuf Ahmed, the Supreme Court had already annulled the elections of 30 July in the federal member state of Galmudug. A new vote was held there on 30 September, and the authorities complied.
